transcript: Yesterday, I saw Corruption at Lincoln Center Theater. This is a new play that tells the story of Tom Watson's crusade to expose the phone hacking that occurred under Rupert Murdoch's media empire in the early 2010s. This is all I knew about it going in, and I figured the themes of the play would be quite relevant, but I wasn't really sure how well it would keep my attention from a storytelling perspective. Thankfully, it totally succeeded in that. It’s very plot driven, and actually very little time is given to character development. But the performances are great and you can tell that the actors have done their due diligence in developing the characters behind the scenes. It is almost three hours long, but it doesn't drag — the scenes are relatively brief and are bookended by meticulously choreographed set changes involving a set of versatile tables. The direction is very brisk and punchy, and gives space for the many nuggets of commentary around journalism, truth, and of course corruption. If the subject matter doesn't interest you at all, I don't know if this play is for you. But then again, I don't feel like I have a ton of stakes in it and I found it pretty compelling. Corruption is actually still in previews, but will be running through April 14th. With that, another playbill for my collection.
